═══ THE ADMIRALTY ═══
Late September 1805
The fleet, the blockades, the crossings — and every order the sea will take. Keys 1–8 turn the ledger's books (Alt+1–8 while you type).
  Fleet: 45 sail of the line — readiness 70  (Adm. Villeneuve)
  Posture: guard — home waters covered
  Yards: Bordelais, Brittany, Normandy, Provence  (0/1 keels this turn)

Orders to the Admiralty
    Blockade the enemy    closes Austria and Russia — not Britain (32 against her, 125 needed)
    The Grand Diversion    45 in 100 at readiness 70 — and again 4 turns after, whatever the outcome; no army is staged to use the open water; a success opens London-Normandy for both turns of the window
    Lay down ships (400g at Bordelais)    a keel joins the fleet at green readiness

  The expedition — the next step:
    Commission Oudinot (3,500g)    Commissioning Oudinot costs 3,500g — the treasury holds 800g.

  The Continental System: 38% of the Continent's ports closed — not yet biting
  Next notch at 40% — 1 more port closed to them.
  Britain would be shut out of the Congress of Paris at 13 of 26 ports (10 now) with no British corps on the Continent — 3 more ports to close.

The Blockade Board
  France — blockaded by Britain: trade halved (−175/turn), the fleet pinned in port
  Holland — blockaded by Britain: the fleet pinned in port
  Spain — blockaded by Britain: trade halved (−100/turn), the fleet pinned in port

The Crossings
  Cagliari–Corsica: SHUT — the Royal Navy at 1.9×
  Corsica–Piedmont: SHUT — the Royal Navy at 1.9×
  London–Normandy: SHUT — the Royal Navy at 1.9×
  crimson = shut · amber = defended shore · gold = window. A shut crossing opens by building or pooling a fleet — or a small expedition slips past it.

The Grand Diversion  ("order the diversion")
  + a fleet in commission
  + at war with a naval power
  + the fleet free to sail the feint (again 4 turns after the last)

The Expedition  ("land <marshal> in <province>")
  + a dockyard under our flag (to embark from home soil)  Bordelais, Brittany, Normandy, Provence
  x a corps of 15,000 men or fewer at a yard, or on a foreign shore  only Napoleon's Guard is under the 15,000 lift, and the Emperor does not sail on an expedition — a new marshal's 5,000-man corps is under it from the day he is raised
  · odds fall with corps size and the hostile fleet's effective strength — effective = sail × readiness
  · a failed run: intercepted ~30% of the corps lost, turned back ~5% — and the fleet's readiness −10 if she is turned back

  Posture: guard — home waters covered
  Yards: Bordelais, Brittany, Normandy, Provence  (0/1 keels this turn)

Orders to the Admiralty
    Blockade the enemy    closes Austria and Russia — not Britain (32 against her, 125 needed)
    The Grand Diversion    45 in 100 at readiness 70 — and again 4 turns after, whatever the outcome; no army is staged to use the open water; a success opens London-Normandy for both turns of the window
    Lay down ships (400g at Bordelais)    a keel joins the fleet at green readiness

  The expedition — the next step:
    Commission Oudinot (3,500g)    Commissioning Oudinot costs 3,500g — the treasury holds 800g.

  The Continental System: 38% of the Continent's ports closed — not yet biting
  Next notch at 40% — 1 more port closed to them.
  Britain would be shut out of the Congress of Paris at 13 of 26 ports (10 now) with no British corps on the Continent — 3 more ports to close.

The Blockade Board
  France — blockaded by Britain: trade halved (−175/turn), the fleet pinned in port
  Holland — blockaded by Britain: the fleet pinned in port
  Spain — blockaded by Britain: trade halved (−100/turn), the fleet pinned in port

The Crossings
  Cagliari–Corsica: SHUT — the Royal Navy at 1.9×
  Corsica–Piedmont: SHUT — the Royal Navy at 1.9×
  London–Normandy: SHUT — the Royal Navy at 1.9×
  crimson = shut · amber = defended shore · gold = window. A shut crossing opens by building or pooling a fleet — or a small expedition slips past it.

The Grand Diversion  ("order the diversion")
  + a fleet in commission
  + at war with a naval power
  + the fleet free to sail the feint (again 4 turns after the last)

The Expedition  ("land <marshal> in <province>")
  + a dockyard under our flag (to embark from home soil)  Bordelais, Brittany, Normandy, Provence
  x a corps of 15,000 men or fewer at a yard, or on a foreign shore  only Napoleon's Guard is under the 15,000 lift, and the Emperor does not sail on an expedition — a new marshal's 5,000-man corps is under it from the day he is raised
  · odds fall with corps size and the hostile fleet's effective strength — effective = sail × readiness
  · a failed run: intercepted ~30% of the corps lost, turned back ~5% — and the fleet's readiness −10 if she is turned back

Your marshals — loyalty, glory, and grievance. Gold answers loyalty; only glory answers envy. Press G to close.

  THE EMPEROR
 
[8] Napoleon  [Infantry]  France
Emperor of the French, on the Rhine with the Guard - 10,000 men carved from Soult's own IV Corps, and Soult's corps is drawn up beside them. He left Paris on the 24th of September and the army is across the river; Mack sits at Ulm one march east. The Grande Armee is his instrument; the Empire is his estate; the marshals shine only in his light - or out of it.
Sovereign: You, in the field. He never objects — his orders are your own will, and cost 1 AP, not 2 (with the live parser, a delegated order such as 'deal with Mack' is read back to you by Berthier for its target before he marches). Where he stands, every corps of his nation fights +10% harder on attack and defence, and enemy commanders will not accept odds against him that they would take against any marshal. But victories won under his eye are HIS: marshals beside him earn half the glory, so ambition needs a command of its own. He holds no rank on the ladder, expects no reward, and cannot be replaced.
Infantry: Standard movement range of 1. Reliable in all terrain. No special restrictions.

  Strength: 10,000 / 10,000  Morale: 85%  Range: 1
     Tactical 10  combat dice (+1 per 3 pts)
     Shock 7  attack damage (+5%/pt)
     Defense 7  damage resistance (-5%/pt)
     Logistics 8  answers the guns (+5 muster/pt)
     Administration 9  recruit pricing (thrifty 8+, wasteful 3-)
     Command 10  rally & recovery (fast 8+, poor 3-)
  The Intendance: raises recruits 15% under standard cost.
  The Rally: reforms beaten armies at double pace — retreat and broken recovery advance 2 stages/turn.
  The Presence  Every French corps fighting in the Emperor's province gains +10% attack and defense. Enemy commanders will not attack his army at odds they would accept against any marshal.

  Trust: 100 (Loyal)  Vindication: 0  Record: 0W/0L
      Reward…    The Empire is his estate.
  Location: Lorraine  Stance: Neutral
    Fortify      Drill   Mack is at Swabia, one region away
  Relationships: Lannes: Friendly (+1), Davout: Friendly (+1), Murat: Friendly (+1), Bernadotte: Hostile (-2)

  OUR DOCTRINE — The Corps System
  "The corps march apart and fight together - and eat what the country gives them."

  Flaw — Living off the land: outside the homeland, in poor or stripped country (war damage ≥ 25%), the army draws 80% of its supply  (uncured — the Train des Équipages would end it once the Grand Quartier Général stands)

Chancery of Helvetia (Dove) of Switzerland

  - Grant it, and Switzerland's tribute of 225g a turn is remitted for 8 collections (1800g forgone): loyalty +0 (its loyalty is already full), its bond with us rises 0 → 20 (worth +1 a turn in loyalty, now +0), for 1 DP.

Your marshals — loyalty, glory, and grievance. Gold answers loyalty; only glory answers envy. Press G to close.

  THE EMPEROR
 
[8] Napoleon  [Infantry]  France
Emperor of the French, on the Rhine with the Guard - 10,000 men carved from Soult's own IV Corps, and Soult's corps is drawn up beside them. He left Paris on the 24th of September and the army is across the river; Mack sits at Ulm one march east. The Grande Armee is his instrument; the Empire is his estate; the marshals shine only in his light - or out of it.
Sovereign: You, in the field. He never objects — his orders are your own will, and cost 1 AP, not 2 (with the live parser, a delegated order such as 'deal with Mack' is read back to you by Berthier for its target before he marches). Where he stands, every corps of his nation fights +10% harder on attack and defence, and enemy commanders will not accept odds against him that they would take against any marshal. But victories won under his eye are HIS: marshals beside him earn half the glory, so ambition needs a command of its own. He holds no rank on the ladder, expects no reward, and cannot be replaced.
Infantry: Standard movement range of 1. Reliable in all terrain. No special restrictions.

═══ THE ADMIRALTY ═══
Early July 1806
The fleet, the blockades, the crossings — and every order the sea will take. Keys 1–8 turn the ledger's books (Alt+1–8 while you type).
  Fleet: 45 sail of the line — readiness 50  (Adm. Villeneuve)
  Posture: guard — home waters covered
  Yards: Bordelais, Brittany, Normandy, Provence  (0/1 keels this turn)

Orders to the Admiralty
    Blockade the enemy    closes Austria and Russia — not Britain (22 against her, 125 needed)
    The Grand Diversion    25 in 100 at readiness 50 — and again 4 turns after, whatever the outcome; no army is staged to use the open water; even a success leaves London-Normandy shut — 27 effective against 50, and 45 is the least that opens it; staging the camp lifts the blockade and readiness recovers +5/turn to 75
    Lay down ships (400g at Bordelais)    a keel joins the fleet at green readiness

  The expedition — the next step:
    Murat, march to Normandy    8,108 men, 4 provinces to the yard — he embarks there
    Lannes, march to Normandy    6,639 men, 4 provinces to the yard — he embarks there

  The Continental System: 27% of the Continent's ports closed — not yet biting
  Next notch at 40% — 4 more ports closed to them.
  Britain would be shut out of the Congress of Paris at 13 of 26 ports (7 now) with no British corps on the Continent — today Paget at Berry keeps the Continent open to her.

The Blockade Board
  France — blockaded by Britain: trade halved (−175/turn), the fleet pinned in port
  Holland — blockaded by Britain: the fleet pinned in port

The Crossings
  Corsica–Piedmont: OPEN — uncovered
  London–Normandy: SHUT — the Royal Navy at 3.7×
  crimson = shut · amber = defended shore · gold = window. A shut crossing opens by building or pooling a fleet — or a small expedition slips past it.

The Grand Diversion  ("order the diversion")
  + a fleet in commission
  + at war with a naval power
  + the fleet free to sail the feint (again 4 turns after the last)

The Expedition  ("land <marshal> in <province>")
  + a dockyard under our flag (to embark from home soil)  Bordelais, Brittany, Normandy, Provence
  x a corps of 15,000 men or fewer at a yard, or on a foreign shore  Massena commands 21,067 — 6,067 over the lift, and a garrison sheds only 3,000 at a time
  · odds fall with corps size and the hostile fleet's effective strength — effective = sail × readiness
  · a failed run: intercepted ~30% of the corps lost, turned back ~5% — and the fleet's readiness −10 if she is turned back

  Chief of Staff Berthier reporting

texts.text:
THE FUNERAL
In late September 1805, at Swabia, the Emperor was killed in the fighting, his corps annihilated by Austria. France has no heir; within the week the Senate declared the Empire at an end. He lay in state in Paris, and the city that had cheered his coronation walked past the bier in silence.

Davout and Lannes stood at the bier. Bernadotte had long since stopped answering his letters.

In 1 battle the Empire won 0 and lost 1; 9 of the enemy fell against 23 of our own. The Battle of Swabia was the worst day. One coalition stood against him — the Third Coalition.

The Verdict of History: the eclipse. Berthier closed the last order book and did not open another.

THE RECORD
The realm at the end: 28 provinces of 126.
Battles fought: 1 — won 0, lost 1 (1 with the Emperor present).
Men lost: 23 · men inflicted: 9.
Provinces taken: 0 · lost: 0.
Marshals: 1 marshal fallen.
Coalitions faced: 1 (Third Coalition) · peaces signed: 0.
Worst defeat: Battle of Swabia (turn 1) — 23 of our own fell.

THE VERDICT OF HISTORY
THE ECLIPSE
The Empire has lost its Emperor, whatever ground it holds.
Its enemies have learned that it can be beaten.
History will call it the beginning of the end.
The Verdict of History: the eclipse.

THE EXILE
In early February 1806, the Empire fell. The Emperor, taken in late September 1805, had been a prisoner of Austria for 10 turns, and Paris stopped waiting. Austria sent him to the fortress of Olmütz — where Austria once kept Lafayette, and knew how to keep a man.

Davout and Lannes asked to share his captivity, and were refused. Bernadotte had long since stopped answering his letters.

One coalition stood against him — the Third Coalition.

The Verdict of History: the eclipse. Metternich, with perfect politeness: "A small inconvenience of residence. The air at Olmütz is said to be bracing."

Emperor of the French, on the Rhine with the Guard - 10,000 men carved from Soult's own IV Corps, and Soult's corps is drawn up beside them. He left Paris on the 24th of September and the army is across the river; Mack sits at Ulm one march east. The Grande Armee is his instrument; the Empire is his estate; the marshals shine only in his light - or out of it.

Where he stands, every corps of his nation fights +10% harder on attack and defence, and enemy commanders will not accept odds against him that they would take against any marshal.
